clue.text: Determined certain content of alcohol

indicators.note: the content of a vessel sits inside it, so the word for certain goes inside the drink

parts.note: mead is an alcoholic drink made from honey
certain means sure

explanation.surface: Someone has worked out how much alcohol a drink contains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content of' makes SURE the filling of MEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Measured and determined both describe something resolute and deliberate, as in a determined or measured response.

clue.text: Recording provided zero state at centre of quake

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
provided means if, as a condition
zero looks like the letter O
Cal is an abbreviation for the US state of California

explanation.surface: A recording made at the heart of an earthquake, on condition there is no movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Epifocal is the geologist's word for lying at the epicentre, the point above an earthquake's focus.

clue.text: Symptom of cold, harsh change when leader's ousted

parts.note: harsh means stern

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, which is thrown out here

parts.note: a mutation is a change

explanation.surface: A doctor describes a cold's symptom and a harsh change of government after a leader's removal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when leader's ousted' removes M from MUTATION, leaving UTATION. Sternutation is the formal word for sneezing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sternutation is sneezing, which a head cold commonly brings on.

clue.text: Fantastic sister to fellow poet

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something wild and fanciful, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remarkable sister to a brother who is also a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fantastic' rearranges SISTER and TO. Fittingly, Christina Rossetti was the sister of the poet and painter Dante Gabriel Rossetti.
explanation.definitionFit: Christina Rossetti was a Victorian poet, sister of the poet Dante Gabriel Rossetti, hence a fellow poet.

clue.text: Cheesemakers ensure ventilation is passing round

indicators.note: round says the word for is passing wraps around the airing word

parts.note: dies means is passing away
to air a room is to ensure it is ventilated

explanation.surface: Cheesemakers making sure fresh air circulates around their stores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is passing' reads as part of the airing picture, but it is the dying word that goes 'round' the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Dairies are farms or plants where milk is turned into butter and cheese.

clue.text: Something for tying up horses

definitions.meaning: cord or twine used to tie parcels
a stable's racehorses are collectively its ...

explanation.surface: Rope for tethering horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Twine for tying parcels, and the racing term for the group of horses kept by one trainer.

clue.text: One of several delivered in twenty two

indicators.note: in says the answer sits within the solution to the clue numbered twenty two

parts.note: the clue refers to the answer at 22 across, which is squint

explanation.surface: A baby born among a multiple birth, delivered at twenty-two weeks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twenty two' is not a number to use but the answer to 22 across, SQUINT; 'in' says the answer lies within it, so drop the outer S and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A quin is one of five babies born at one birth, a quintuplet.

clue.text: Took up dope and uses madly

indicators.note: madly signals letters thrown into a frenzied new order

explanation.surface: Someone started taking drugs and used them wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly' is the anagram signal; 'and' joins the two fodder words and supplies no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse a cause is to adopt or embrace it.

clue.text: Opposed to endless search for period pieces

parts.note: anti means opposed to

indicators.note: endless says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a quest is a search

explanation.surface: Someone is against a never-ending hunt for old objects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts the T from QUEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiques are old furniture or objects from a past era, called period pieces.

clue.text: Dance judge I have got to

parts.note: 've is the contracted form of have

explanation.surface: A judge confesses to having taken up dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Jive is a lively swing dance of the 1940s and 50s.

clue.text: Rome riotings set off campaign for union

indicators.note: set off as if by an explosion, the letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Riots in Rome spark a political campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set off' rearranges ROME and RIOTINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Risorgimento was the nineteenth-century movement that unified Italy into one state.

clue.text: More ordinary? No, out of this world

parts.note: extra means more
mundane means ordinary

explanation.surface: Is it even more humdrum? No, it is otherworldly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' corrects the surface reading: EXTRA MUNDANE is not more ordinary but beyond the mundane world.
explanation.definitionFit: Extramundane means beyond the physical world, transcending ordinary material existence.

clue.text: One in charge of sect that's secret

parts.note: OC is Officer Commanding, the person in charge of a military unit
a cult is a sect

explanation.surface: The leader of a religious group that operates in secrecy.
explanation.definitionFit: Occult knowledge is hidden, esoteric and kept from the uninitiated.

clue.text: Period that's most important, if extremely short

indicators.note: short at both extremes, so the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: weightiest means most important

explanation.surface: A brief era that matters more than any other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely short' trims W and T from the ends of WEIGHTIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighties is a decade, a span of history such as 1980 to 1989.

clue.text: Jump in to attack run-down cinema

indicators.note: in tells us the word for jump goes inside the word for attack

parts.note: a fit is an attack, as of coughing
leap means jump

explanation.surface: Someone leaps into action to assault a shabby picture house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. A fleapit is British slang for a scruffy old cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleapit is British slang for a shabby, grubby old picture house.

clue.text: At all times probing angle that's highly charged

indicators.note: probing means poking inside, so the always word goes into the angling word

parts.note: to angle is to fish
ever means at all times

explanation.surface: A constant probing from one angle makes a situation tense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'probing' is the container signal; 'angle' is the verb, to fish with a rod, not a corner.
explanation.definitionFit: A feverish atmosphere is frantic and intensely excited, charged with emotion.

clue.text: Retiring party took steps to obtain lobster

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the party and the steps are both read in reverse

parts.note: a do is a party
paced means walked in measured steps

explanation.surface: Someone leaving a party walked off to fetch a lobster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' reverses DOPACED as a whole to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A decapod is a ten-legged crustacean, the order to which lobsters belong.

clue.text: From on high, English tactics must be revised

indicators.note: revised means altered, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: From the top, English tactics need a rethink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be revised' is the anagram signal, giving CSTATIC after the E. 'From' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a high means being elated, exhilarated, overjoyed.

clue.text: Application in the post missing a couple of pages

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so these letters are taken out

parts.note: a post is a job, an appointment
A for a, and PP, the abbreviation for pages, two of them

explanation.surface: A letter arrives in the post with two pages missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes A and PP from APPOINTMENT. 'in the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical cream or salve is something applied to the skin, an application.

clue.text: Your body's fat? Cry uncontrollably

definitions.meaning: the fatty layer of a whale or a person
to sob noisily and without restraint

explanation.surface: A body-conscious person in tears over their weight.
explanation.definitionFit: The thick fat layer of a whale, or slangily a person, and the verb for weeping noisily.

clue.text: Named wine from French region I brought back after delay

parts.note: the Var is a department of southern France

indicators.note: brought back means returned, so the delay word is read backwards

parts.note: late means arriving after a delay

explanation.surface: A wine named after a French region, which I brought home late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns LATE into ETAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A varietal is a wine made from, and labelled with, a single grape variety.

clue.text: Hair tinting is popular within Chinese society

indicators.note: within tells us the popular word goes inside the society word

parts.note: a tong is a Chinese secret society
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A hair colouring that is fashionable among Chinese people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' is the container signal. A tong is a Chinese secret society or guild.
explanation.definitionFit: Toning is colouring the hair with a mild tint that adjusts its shade.

clue.text: Quick look shows spades — a good run of the same suit

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for spades in card games

parts.words: a good run of the same suit
parts.note: in piquet a quint is a sequence of five cards in one suit

explanation.surface: A card player glances at a hand holding a strong spade sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: QUINT is a card term from piquet, a five-card run in a suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A squint is slang for a brief glance, as in having a squint at something.

clue.text: Feature of old car company chairman's job

definitions.meaning: the footboard along the side of a vintage motor car
a chairman's task is managing the directors

explanation.surface: Part of a vintage car and the role of a company head.
explanation.definitionFit: A step along the side of vintage cars, and read as two words, managing a company's directors.

clue.text: Spy sees six leaving Norwegian port

indicators.note: leaving says these letters depart from the port's name

parts.note: Narvik is a port in northern Norway
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An agent watches six people depart from a harbour in Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' removes VI from NARVIK. Nark is British slang for a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nark is a police informer, someone who spies and tells tales.

clue.text: Noise of rotating shaft could make one jump

indicators.note: noise of says we want what a word sounds like when spoken

parts.note: an axle is a rotating shaft on which wheels turn

explanation.surface: A squealing spinning shaft could startle someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make one' is a link; the surface's sense of jumping in fright misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: An axel is a figure-skating leap with one and a half turns in the air.

clue.text: Tender for exterior of city university

indicators.note: the tender word serves as the outside of the city word

parts.note: tender means sore
Bonn is a city in Germany

explanation.surface: A bid to supply the outside of a city campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for exterior of' is the container signal. 'Tender' looks like a bid but means painful.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sorbonne is the historic seat of the University of Paris.

clue.text: Engineers make a fuss if having to design again

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
to create is British slang for making a fuss

explanation.surface: Engineers kick up a fuss if they must redo a design.
explanation.definitionFit: To recreate something is to make it anew, producing it once more.
